en: The Great Cloud Sutra on Non-conceptualization, Scroll Nine.
[Missing Text] ... out of a heart of compassion, accept us... [Missing Text] ... at this time.

Regarding the aforementioned: by means of the mind that has committed various offenses, even grave sins shall be extinguished, and wholesome dharmas will gradually arise; through this, immeasurable sentient beings shall attain rootless faith.
Immeasurable [and] ... sentient beings have resolved their minds toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. ... [omitted].
At that time, there was a brahmin in the assembly named Ṛjumārga. He rose from his seat, raised his hands in astonishment, and spoke these words:
"The great assembly all knows that the śramaṇa Gautama is a great liar."
I have previously and constantly said:

"Those who commit the five heinous crimes, slander the True Dharma, revile the noble ones, misappropriate the property of the Saṃgha of the Four Quarters or the property of the Buddha-Dharma, violate the four grave prohibitions, defile bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs, and hold false views—these ten kinds of people are of the lineage of hell."
"Previously, one could not sever the fetters of the desire realm, realize the fruits of the śramaṇa, nor increase the unsurpassed True Dharma.
Now, however, it is said:
"If one possesses right faith and repents for what was previously done, then one's offenses will be extinguished, and one can once again increase the Tathāgata’s True Dharma."
"Those who lack faith are called people of hell;
those who possess right faith are called those who abide according to the Dharma.
Why, Gautama, do you make these two kinds of statements?
"To have faith in my Dharma is called right view;
not to have faith in my Dharma is called wrong view.
The śramaṇa Gautama disregards his previous statement and again speaks these words:"
"If all things are thus, how can he be called 'All-Knowing' (Sarvajña)?
Śramaṇa Gautama, you are not all-knowing and do not possess all-seeing; yet you claim to teach all-seeing."
The various non-Buddhists also say this:
"I am all-knowing; I am all-seeing.
Those who believe in my path are said to possess right view."
"To have faith in Gautama is called a false view.
What is the difference between these two statements?
If there is no difference, how can one distinguish which is correct and which is false?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Great Cloud Secret Treasury,
saying: “Good son,
listen attentively, listen attentively!
All sentient beings are surrounded by the four inversions, and further possess four incomplete dharmas, namely: precepts, views, deportment, and right livelihood.

"Because of these eight dharmas, sentient beings are led to walk in the realm of darkness, unable to distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox, or between the Dharma and what is not the Dharma. Good son!"
The brahmin Ajita, in the midst of the great assembly, raised his hand in alarm and said:
"The śramaṇa Gautama speaks falsehoods.
These words were immediately proven false.
"Good son! All dharmas are empty; the Tathāgata is able to speak of them, and for this reason, the Tathāgata does not speak falsely.

All dharmas have no nature, no fixedness, no substance, and no conditions; they cannot be definitively described. They are empty, without arising or ceasing, and are not called 'things. They are neither pure nor impure, like a dream, like an illusion, like the moon in water, like a mirage in the heat, like an echo, like a city of the Gandharvas, like the hair of a tortoise, or like the horns of a rabbit."
The essence of greed, hatred, and delusion has no reality; they arise due to unwholesome conceptualization.
Originally non-existent, they now exist; having existed, they return to non-existence.
"Good son! All sentient beings do not understand these signs; therefore, they proclaim:
'The śramaṇa Gautama speaks two kinds of words, speaking falsely.'"
"Although the Tathāgata has spoken of these ten kinds of sentient beings, those who believe shall be able to eliminate all their transgressions;
those who do not give rise to faith shall enter hell."
"Good son!
If there is a sinner who can contemplate the characteristics of dharmas in this way, that person is called one with faith and is able to extinguish all sins;
if they cannot contemplate in this way, they are called one without faith and are a person destined for hell."

“Good son! There is the Lion’s Roar, the Unsurpassed Ladder of Wisdom, the Dharma-gate of the Dhāraṇī of Boundless Spiritual Footings that returns one to the patience of non-arising. If a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva brings this dhāraṇī to maturity, then by proclaiming a single verse within a great assembly, he can utterly destroy all false views and shatter the inverted mind along with its mental factors;
he leaves behind all doubt and is able to break through the defilements of stinginess, greed, hatred, and ignorance.”

“Good son! If there is another person who, though possessing immeasurable sins, hears and upholds this [dhāraṇī], and for seven days recollects the Buddha with a sincere mind—without thinking of any worldly affairs or the fetters of afflictions—that person will immediately see all the three realms, the three periods of time, and the aggregates, bases, and elements.

Just as a great wind, at that moment their mind is like the wind; they contemplate all phenomena—the three realms, the three periods of time, and the aggregates, bases, and elements—without any attachment whatsoever, which is beyond verbal description.”
Such a person is said to be unattached to the three realms, the aggregates, the sense bases, and the elements.

When practicing this contemplation, within the three realms, they are not called pure, nor are they called impure; they are not called liberated, nor are they called bound; they are not called "this," nor are they called "that"; they are not called an ordinary person, nor are they called a sage; they are not called departing, nor are they called abiding.
Such a person will never again be deceived or deluded by the dharmas of ordinary worldlings;
they sever all conceptualizations, including the inversion of views and the inversion of mind, and regard the pleasures of the five desires as being like the wind or empty space.

Although he conforms to worldly conventions and speaks of the existence of the five desires, his inner mind remains entirely unstained by them; being neither born nor extinguished, he is able to sever all unwholesome dharmas, as previously described regarding the ten kinds of sentient beings.
“Good son! Because this brahmin does not understand, he proclaims these words:
‘The śramaṇa Gautama speaks in two ways; his teachings are false.’”
“Good son! If a person can contemplate the characteristics of dharmas in this way, that person will immediately attain the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
If one attains this patience, you should know that such a person will certainly achieve the fruit of the unsurpassed path.”

If there are good men or good women who obtain such dharani-gates, and with joyful hearts recite and praise them, mindfully honoring the Triple Gem and making offerings with utmost sincerity, these people shall be revered by all humans and devas, and shall also be protected by the Four Great Heavenly Kings among the devas and humans.

Although they have not yet attained liberation, they are also able to eliminate all grave offenses—the obstacle of karma, the obstacle of afflictions, the obstacle of retribution, and the obstacle of dharmas.
Even in their dreams, they shall never lose the bodhicitta.
Fully possessing the four kinds of unimpeded knowledge (*pratisaṃvid*), they are unsullied by worldly dharmas, just like a lotus flower.
Free from all fears, the four Māras, their great enemies, cannot do them harm.
They are able to increase wholesome dharmas; whatever they speak, the assembly joyfully listens to and receives.
All who see them give rise to compassion, and having given rise to compassion, they are able to rescue [others].
They remain far removed from heterodox texts and unwholesome, evil friends.
One’s body shall be free from the four hundred and four diseases, and one will be able to relieve all the afflictions and sufferings of sentient beings.
One will constantly bestow joy and happiness upon sentient beings.
In whatever place one is born, all the sense faculties will be complete and intact.
The four immeasurable minds cannot be shaken or diverted.
Seeing those who are terrified, he gives rise to compassionate concern for them as if they were his own parents, constantly acting for the sake of sentient beings.
They delight in being seen and cherished; though they do not crave profit, they are honored and supported by all.
They remain far removed from the five hindrances and delight in conforming to wholesome dharmas.
If, due to external circumstances, they sleep for a short time, they will see, within their dreams, the Tathāgatas and various Bodhisattvas of the ten directions.

In this way, the Bodhisattva, for those who had never before heard the Dharma, caused them all to hear it; he distinguished between the ten wholesome and ten unwholesome dharmas, revealed the suffering of birth and death, opened the great skillful means, and expounded the Bodhisattva precepts.

Having heard the Dharma, they immediately give rise to joy and faith; by virtue of these causes and conditions, at the time of their death, their minds do not regress, they feel no fear, they behold the Buddhas of the ten directions, and their words are never erroneous. Upon casting off the body, they immediately attain rebirth in a pure and wondrous land, where they behold the Buddhas and hear the Dharma.
They constantly draw near to the Buddhas, cultivate the five supernormal powers, and practice spontaneous birth, which is not obtained through others.
They always attain transformation-birth and never enter the three evil realms.
They shall not fail to see the Buddha, shall delight in hearing the True Dharma, and shall make offerings to the Saṃgha. "Why is this?
O son of good family!
This dharma-gate of dhāraṇī was proclaimed by all the Buddhas of the past for the purpose of extinguishing the sins of sentient beings in the degenerate age.
All the Buddhas of the past clearly and joyfully beheld it.

In future ages, there will be various evil sentient beings who are unable to draw near to virtuous spiritual friends; they will stray from the right path, walk in darkness, cultivate false views, and dwell perpetually within the grave illness of afflictions, thereby departing from the path to Bodhi.
For this reason, all the Buddhas of the past have together expounded this dhāraṇī.
Son of good family!
If there are Buddhas of the present in the ten directions, they too shall together proclaim this dhāraṇī.
If there are all the Buddhas of the ten directions in the future, they too shall together proclaim this dhāraṇī, so that all may together extinguish [the offenses], O Brahmin Zhidao!
Because of such equal transgressions against the precepts.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the brahmin Ajita:
"Noble son! You have said:..."
"The five great elements of sentient beings are called the five aggregates (skandhas), the twelve bases (āyatanas), and the eighteen realms (dhātus).
Within these five aggregates, and even within these eighteen realms, sentient beings fall into perversion and give rise to the notion of a self (ātman);
because of this notion of a self, they transmigrate through birth and death like the turning of a wheel.

Due to these four inversions, sentient beings are born blind and die blind, undergoing immeasurable suffering; they are deprived of the joys of humans and devas as well as unsurpassed bliss, and their minds lack shame, remorse, right faith, and wisdom.
Therefore, it is said:
"The four great elements, the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen realms are the self and what belongs to the self.
O son of good family!
"I now ask you; answer as you see fit.
Is the earth element in your doctrine identical with the self or belonging to the self?
"No, World-Honored One."
"Because of this earth element, there is a self. "Good son!
If the self exists because of the earth element, then the self is the earth, and the earth is the self."

Therefore, earth is called "earth," and it is also called "self," "sentient being," "life-span," "vessel of desire," "growth," "person" (*puruṣa*), "youth" (*māṇava*), "doer," "one who causes to do," "ariser," "one who causes to arise," "speaker," "one who causes to speak," "experiencer," "one who causes to experience," "knower," and "one who causes to know. The other great elements (*mahābhūta*) and the sphere of mental objects (*dharmāyatana-dhātu*) are likewise so named.
Good son! All the aggregates, sense bases, and elements are not called "self," and even that which causes one to know is not called "self. Good son!
All the great elements, aggregates, sense bases, and realms—past, future, and present—are not the self, nor do they belong to a self.
Therefore, these great elements, aggregates, sense bases, and realms cannot be grasped or maintained; they are neither born nor extinguished, they are unconditioned, and they cannot be seen or heard.

Good son! The eye is empty, forms are empty, and eye-consciousness is empty; the contact conditioned by these three factors is also empty, and the sensation conditioned by these four factors is also empty.
Therefore, all dharmas have no master; they lack autonomy, being neither this nor that. Good son!
Thus, these great aggregates, bases, and elements are neither male nor female; the mind and mental factors are not called male, nor are they called female.
For these reasons, all phenomena are like space; arising and ceasing moment by moment, they lack intrinsic nature and are therefore like flashes of lightning, beyond description.
“If a person kills another and incurs the offense of killing, does that person incur the offense through their present body and mind,
or through their past body and mind,
or through their future body and mind?”
The brahmin said:
“World-Honored One!
The past has already ceased;”
"The future has not yet arisen;
the present does not abide.
The Buddha said:
"For this reason, there should be no sin of killing.
If one says that killing exists, how can it be called 'killing'?
Earth does not kill earth; the same applies to all other elements, aggregates, bases, and realms."
The brahmin said:
“World-Honored One!
Because of an evil mind through causes and conditions, it is called ‘killing.’”
The Buddha said, "Good son,
why do you say that one is called a 'killer' because of an evil mind?"
Where does such an evil mind abide?
Does it reside in the desire realm, the form realm, or the formless realm?
Or does it abide in empty space?
Is it the mind-element?
Is it the conditioned element?
Or is it the realm of non-perception?
Is it the realm with outflows?
Is it the realm without outflows?
Is it the realm of existence?
"Is it without boundaries? Good son!
If there is someone who gives rise to an evil mind and commits the five heinous crimes, who is it that gives rise to them?"
As for such a mind, what is its nature?
Who turns this mind to perform what is wholesome or unwholesome?
Abiding in what place does it undergo such transformation?
"If there is neither an agent nor an experiencer, how can you say that there is a self and what belongs to a self?
At that time, the brahmin remained silent and said nothing.
“Good son! For what reason do you remain silent and not answer?
The brahmin said:
“World-Honored One!
I have now attained entry into this Dharma-gate and see all phenomena as being without action, without grasping, without abiding, without nature, and without essence, and thus inexpressible;
they are like space, like a mirage in the heat, like a dream, or like the moon reflected in water.”
World-Honored One!
All dharmas have no place of abiding; there is neither "that" nor "this.
For this reason, I now remain silent and without speech.
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent!
O son of good family!"

This is called the Lion’s Roar, the Unsurpassed Ladder of Wisdom; it is the Dharma-gate of the Dharani of Boundless Divine Footsteps and Dharma Practices that returns one to the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). It severs all suffering, enters the gate of great wisdom, and is the initial practice of the path to Bodhi. It cuts off the two kinds of birth and distances one from the dust and grime of afflictions (*kleśa*).
This Dharma gate is not shared with any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
"Good sons! Even if you were to kill your father or kill your mother, you would only incur heavy karma, but you would not commit a heinous crime (ānantarya-karma)."
"You have now further attained entry into this Dharma-gate and given rise to great faith; gradually you shall attain its complete and total eradication.
Having heard this, the Brahmin was filled with great joy. He immediately stepped forward to prostrate before the Buddha, knelt with palms joined, and addressed the Buddha, saying:

"World-Honored One, I was dull-witted and ignorant, slandering what the Buddha had spoken. Now, for the sake of my transgressions and the fault of slandering the Buddha, I sincerely repent before the Tathāgata."
“Good son! Do you now wish to retain any remnant of this transgression?
“World-Honored One!”
"What is meant by 'the remainder'?
Good son, although one may feel shame and remorse, and reveal and repent of one's transgressions, if one does not resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, this is called 'the remainder'."
If one can have compassion for all sentient beings and resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, this is called "without remainder.

Such a person is also able to sever the four inversions, attain noble wisdom, draw near to the Brahma-abodes, increase wholesome dharmas, and possess firm roots of goodness; thus, even though there may be conditions like ice, they cannot cause them to regress, and they shall attain unimpeded wisdom.
At that time, the brahmin Jñānapatha and countless nayutas of sentient beings said to the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
We now, out of sincere compassion for the sake of all sentient beings, resolve our minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and repent of what we have previously done.”
We only pray that the Tathāgata, out of great compassion and pity, will accept our profound repentance.

We further entreat the Tathāgata to speak, for our sake, the Lion’s Roar, the Unsurpassed Ladder of Wisdom, the Dharma-gate of the Reversion to Non-arising Patience, and the Dhāraṇī of Boundless Divine Footsteps.
This dhāraṇī is not shared with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
Even if there were such shared elements, I do not seek them;

what I now seek is the Tathāgata’s dhāraṇī of the ultimate truth and unsurpassed wisdom, which can adorn all wholesome dharmas, all worldly dharmas, and the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed wisdom, fearlessness, giving, and so forth.

For the sake of increasing wholesome dharmas for the great assembly, so that they may not be forgotten or lost, one should receive and uphold them with a sincere heart; this can destroy the four inversions, accomplish the path to Bodhi, and eliminate all fetters and evil karmas.
This dhāraṇī is a great treasury of jewels for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the unsurpassed samādhi.
By these causes and conditions, it enables bodhisattvas to have no regressive thoughts even within their dreams.
Wherever he goes—whether among the assembly of śramaṇas, the assembly of brāhmaṇas, or the assembly of kṣatriyas—his mind is free from fear.
He always delights in giving and practices with diligent perseverance.
They remain far removed from all evil and unwholesome karma;
they are able to inspire a heart of joy in their enemies.
They distance themselves from all negligence, heterodox writings, wrong views, and evil associates, and are likewise able to subdue such individuals.
They are always able to expound the unimpeded Dharma-gate, causing those who preach the Dharma to be free from illness, suffering, and all misfortunes, and not to be taken advantage of by any māras.
They constantly know their past lives;
they attain bodies of miraculous birth and leave behind all evil existences.
They always have the opportunity to draw near to the Buddhas of the ten directions, listen to and receive the True Dharma, and make offerings to the Sangha.
World-Honored One!
This dhāraṇī is named "The Secret Treasury of All Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
We only pray that...
“Tathāgata!
Out of compassion for us, please analyze and explain this.
The Buddha said:
“Excellent, excellent!
Son of good family,
this dhāraṇī is fully capable of accomplishing immeasurable wholesome dharmas, just as has been taught according to the Dharma.”
"Listen attentively, listen attentively!
I shall speak for you.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke as follows:

“Pāre | Kāre | Pākāre | Tākāre | Dhāravijñapti | Prapañcamukha | Prācūṇe | Prāṇe | Vinirjñapti | Śaṇḍe | Prapañcane-tīri | Far removed from form, scent, and taste; far removed from inversion; able to incinerate all poisons; able to distance one from all evil spirits, evil paths, and diseases; the Dharma-gate of non-obstruction; the Dharma-gate of fulfillment; the Dharma-gate of true wisdom; unobstructed mind; the great Dharma-offering; the fulfillment of the Dharma-offering; able to destroy the five hindrances—Svāhā. “Good son! ”
If the disciples of the Buddha—whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—uphold such a dhāraṇī mantra, reciting it, reading it, or transcribing it.

If, on the eighth day of the month, one bathes oneself with purity, puts on new clothes, purifies the inner mind, and recites [this mantra] one thousand times before a Buddha image, a stūpa, or a relic, and ties one hundred and eight knots in a cotton thread to bind the head, this person will be able to remain invisible to all even when traveling with evil crowds, and shall have no bad dreams while sleeping; this is called the single phrase *dhāraṇī*.
“Good son! There is furthermore one phrase, which is as follows:

‘Svā-ni-mu-ni, phala-mu-ni, upa-śānta, ku-sri, kṣaṇa-jña, unshakable mind, firm and solid, like lightning, abiding according to the Dharma, abiding in equanimity, able to give birth to the light of Tathāgata-wisdom, amṛta, vītama-ta, subhūti, mṛdu, unimpeded tranquility, increasing the mind of mindfulness, svāhā. If there is a good son or good daughter...”
“Good woman!
Receive, uphold, recite, and transcribe these dhāraṇī phrases.

Before a Buddha, an image, a stūpa, or śarīra relics, you should recite them one thousand times while drinking black honey, lotus-transformed *māndhuka* gruel. Within a single day, you will be able to recite a thousand verses and attain the knowledge of others' minds.”

"Good son! If there are good men or good women, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who, dwelling in a place of solitude, with sincere hearts and in accordance with the Dharma, practice this dhāraṇī, these persons shall, within no more than seven days, attain the four dhyānas, destroy the fetters of the desire realm, behold the Buddhas of the ten directions, and obtain the samādhi of realized intent. They will be able to transform sentient beings and extinguish all obstacles—namely, the obstacle of karma, the obstacle of retribution, and the obstacle of afflictions;
they will be able to purify the faculties of sentient beings."
It can burn away all the afflictions, inversions, and fetters of sentient beings;
it causes one to draw near to and abide in the path of the noble ones, rendering it impossible for them to regress from bodhi;

it brings one close to omniscience, whereby wisdom arises without depending on external causes, and one attains the dharma-gates of all Buddhas—the unhindered and fearless states throughout the three periods of time.
By the power of the causal conditions of this samādhi, one attains the power of aspiration, whereby one can purify all evil sentient beings and swiftly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
When this dhāraṇī was being spoken, within that great assembly, eighty-four thousand nayutas of sentient beings attained this dhāraṇī;
eight nayutas of sentient beings, having eliminated the causal conditions for heavy karma, attained the patience in accordance with the Dharma (dharmakṣānti);

and immeasurable sentient beings who had not yet resolved upon the path of the śrāvaka were inspired to do so, and those who had not yet resolved upon the path of the pratyekabuddha were likewise inspired.
He causes immeasurable sentient beings who have not yet resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* to so resolve;
he causes immeasurable sentient beings to become non-retrogressive in their resolve for bodhicitta.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Great Cloud Secret Treasury addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

In future ages, if there should be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who receive, uphold, read, and recite this Great Cloud Sūtra, what kind of merit and virtue shall these individuals attain?”
Furthermore, what afflictions can they extinguish?
What karmic retributions can they distance themselves from?
And what power of wisdom do they attain?
When shall I attain the wisdom of the Mahāyāna, by which I may cross the boundless great ocean of birth and death?
When shall I turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma, bestowing upon all sentient beings the pure eye of the Dharma?
The Buddha said,
“Good son! Regarding such matters as these, one should not provide an answer at all.”
The Bodhisattva Mahāmegha made this request three times, yet the Buddha did not answer.
At that time, Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
To whom should such a sutra as this be entrusted to tame all evil sentient beings of future generations?
World-Honored One!
In future ages, there will be outcaste Kṣatriyas, and outcaste Brāhmaṇas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras;
There may be those who have not yet heard such a sutra,
or who inflict evil deeds upon the fourfold assembly.
Due to these karmic conditions, for immeasurable ages they shall undergo this retribution within the three evil realms.
I only pray that the Tathāgata,
for the sake of extinguishing such evil karmic fruits as those of the caṇḍālas, and because of these very fruits, will entrust the sūtras to his attendant.
The Buddha said,
"Mañjuśrī! After my parinirvāṇa, in this buddha-world, the lineage of true kṣatriya kings will be extinguished without remainder."
A base and evil person shall become a king.

Such an evil person severs the true Dharma of kingship; arrogant and envious, his mind lacks shame and remorse; he practices much heedlessness, and though not a proper object of refuge, he acts as one.

In such a land, all the ministers, elders, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and others are likewise: they violate the precepts and are stingy and greedy; their minds lack shame and remorse; they are possessed of the ten unwholesome paths of action; they do not believe in the Three Jewels; they have no intention to make offerings; they are unable to seek [the Dharma] through petition; and they constantly delight in proclaiming that there is neither cause nor effect.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas see that all the sentient beings in this land thus habituate themselves to evil, they immediately transfer to other pure lands.

Once the Bodhisattvas have departed, this world—this evil age and evil time—immediately becomes rampant; sentient beings suffer many diseases, grain becomes exceedingly expensive, and the four armies rise up in competition, plundering one another, all because sentient beings do not know contentment!
“Good son! To whom shall I entrust such a sutra as this?
Who among these evil sentient beings is capable of analyzing and explaining it?”
"Good son!

If there is anyone who can endure hunger and thirst, various afflictions, verbal abuse, and physical blows, and who does not begrudge their own body or life, such a person will be able to disseminate this scripture in future ages."
"If there be such a person, I shall entrust this unsurpassed, true scripture to them!

At that time, within the assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Fearless Merit Swift-March who rose from his seat, prostrated with his head at the Buddha's feet, knelt on both knees, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

Throughout immeasurable lifetimes, I am able to undergo immeasurable suffering—such as having my hands and feet cut off, my head split open, my eyes gouged out, or enduring hunger, thirst, cold, heat, beatings, and abuse—even unto the sufferings of the three evil realms—all for the sake of disseminating this sutra of the Tathāgata.
I am able to penetrate the worlds of the Tathāgatas, including all great cities, villages, towns, and settlements, as well as among dragons and ghosts, to disseminate this sutra.

This is for the sake of severing the four inversions of sentient beings, causing them to uphold the precepts, practice with diligent vigor, be fully endowed with right view, accomplish the six pāramitās, and attain unsurpassed bodhi.
The Buddha said:
“Excellent, excellent!
Son of good family!”
"It shall be as you have wished; you are fully capable of performing the work of a Buddha for immeasurable sentient beings. Good son!
Your aspiration will enable you to fulfill the six pāramitās and swiftly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"Good son!
Although there may be a great multitude of people, those such as yourselves are truly difficult to find;
furthermore, those in future ages who will accept your words will likewise be difficult to find."
Although there may be those who receive [this teaching], it is likewise rare to find those who give rise to profound faith, uphold, read, recite, explain, analyze, and instruct others in it.
If, in future ages, there are those who can receive and uphold it, read and recite it, explain it, transcribe it, and delight in teaching it, such persons shall obtain ten merits:
their bodies will always be free from illness;...
Without seeking, they naturally obtain offerings of clothing, food and drink, bedding, and medicine;
without seeking, they draw near to virtuous friends;
and they are cherished and remembered by all the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Whatever Dharma he preaches, people joyfully listen to and accept;
they attain śamatha and vipaśyanā;
and they become fully endowed with both worldly and world-transcending meanings.
The body and mind are tranquil;
the Three Jewels increase;
and one attains the unsurpassed dhāraṇī.
"Good son!
Although I have spoken of its ten merits, if one can teach others to repent, thereby eliminating immeasurable evil offenses, they will likewise obtain immeasurable merit."
Furthermore, good son!
If such a person can, with a sincere heart, receive, uphold, read, recite, and extensively explain it to others in future ages, they shall obtain immeasurable merit.
When this person gives up their life, they will clearly behold the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Each of those Buddhas will say:
"O virtuous son!..."
Born into my world, they shall hear my True Dharma, sever the four inversions, extinguish all unwholesome dharmas, achieve noble wisdom, and abide in the Brahma-abodes.
Having received my Dharma, they shall always attain birth by transformation, sever the three evil paths, swiftly attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and even enter into great *parinirvāṇa*.
Having heard this, that person gives rise to a heart of joy and immediately attains rebirth in those pure Buddha-lands. "Good son!

Such a person, having received this Dharma, will in every place of rebirth have all faculties complete, obtain a most exquisite and wondrous form, and be one whom all sentient beings delight to behold."
Having attained faith in the Triple Gem, they are able to provide offerings.
If they hear the True Dharma, they immediately attain liberation and destroy all karma.
They firmly uphold the True Dharma they have received without losing it, thereby obtaining all dharani-doors.

The samādhis of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas can transcend the paths of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and furthermore enable them to transform and guide immeasurable sentient beings while abiding in the Brahma-abodes.
"If there are those in the future who receive and uphold these words, they shall attain accomplishment and such merit as this.
Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
Since this bodhisattva is able to give rise to such a rare mind, it is precisely for him that this sutra should be entrusted.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Swift Movement of Fearless Merit:
“I now entrust this sutra to you!”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Swift Movement of Fearless Virtue, together with immeasurable bodhisattvas, reverently received the Buddha’s teaching and accepted this sutra.

Immeasurable Brahmās, such as those dwelling in the Brahma-abodes; immeasurable Śakras, such as Indrānila; immeasurable spirits and deities, such as the Four Heavenly Kings; and immeasurable dragon kings, such as Nanda and Upananda, likewise all received and upheld it together.
Immeasurable sentient beings have resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
This was transcribed on the eleventh day of the first month of the Water-Hare year, having been offered for one year by the laywoman of pure faith, Zhang Xu'ai.
